The product SMILES still not matching. Maybe the product is different: The precursor is an alkene with phenyl and chain ending with carbonyl CF3. The template likely does a hydroxy addition to form a cyclobutane? Actually template appears to be a cyclization: It takes a chain with alkene and carbonyl to form a cyclic alcohol (intramolecular). The product likely is a bicyclic? Let's examine mapped_rxn: Reactant side: ([CH3:1]/[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)=[CH:9]/[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C:13](=[O:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]) This is a molecule with a double bond between C2 (attached to CH3 and phenyl) and CH (C9). Then chain CH2-CH2-CH2-C(=O)-CF3. So it's a linear chain with terminal carbonyl. The product side: ([CH3:1][C@H:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]) So product is a cyclobutane? The atoms 9-10-11-12-13 form a 5-member? Actually C@@H:9 attached to ring atom 1? It shows [C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1... So a 4-member ring? The notation [C@@H:9]1 ... [C@@:13]1 indicates a 4-member ring (atoms 9,10,11,12,13? Wait 5 atoms). The SMILES would be something like C[C@H](c1ccccc1)C1CC C C1(O)C(F)(F)F but with stereochemistry. That we tried.

Maybe the product SMILES is "CC(C1=CC=CC=C1)C1CCC(C1O)C(F)(F)F" (no stereochemistry). Let's test verify_step without stereochemistry.
